excerpt.quote: **Classification: qualified.** The results support the narrower conclusion that these supplied participant maps do not show corrected evidence for a positive vmPFC group effect. All 54 maps are included; the one-sample, equal-participant-weight model and the full-mask one-sided Bonferroni test are defensible conditional on the supplied first-level estimates. The vmPFC sphere mean is -0.0057 model units (95% CI [-0.0323, 0.0210]), *t*(53) = -0.43, one-sided *p* = .664; no voxel in the sphere survives whole-brain correction. This follows the original NARPS instruction to use whole-brain corrected inference ([Hypothesis 1 instructions](https://www.narps.info/files/narps_instructions_for_analysis_teams.pdf)). This is a lack of support for the positive hypothesis, not evidence of a true zero effect or absence of individual responses.

conclusion.quote: The narrow conclusion that these inputs and this group model provide no whole-brain-corrected support for a positive vmPFC response is defensible. All 54 participants were analyzed with no exclusions. The script checked participant/map matching, common image geometry, finite values and input checksums; it used a 90%-coverage search mask (210,968 voxels) and one-sided participant sign-flip max-T correction across that whole mask (9,999 permutations, α=.05). It found 24 corrected voxels in three small posterior occipital components and none in the independently specified 10-mm vmPFC sphere centered at MNI [0, 42, -8]. The descriptive sphere mean was -0.0095 map units (95% t interval [-0.0377, 0.0187]). The relevant results are in [summary.json](/Users/johnlee/.local/state/stamped-in-practice/narps-v1/narps-r1-03/targets/judgment-01/results/summary.json), [report.md](/Users/johnlee/.local/state/stamped-in-practice/narps-v1/narps-r1-03/targets/judgment-01/results/report.md), and the replay figures below. This follows the supplied requirement for whole-brain correction in the [NARPS Hypothesis 1 instructions](https://www.narps.info/files/narps_instructions_for_analysis_teams.pdf).

excerpt.quote: **Classification: supported.** The reported conclusion is a defensible lack of support for a positive vmPFC finding under the required whole-brain family-wise error threshold. The analysis includes all 54 supplied participants without exclusion, checks map identity, checks common image shape/affine and finite values, and limits the search to voxels represented in at least 49 maps. It uses 9,999 participant-level sign flips and the maximum positive t statistic over the full coverage mask. No voxel in the independently defined 10-mm vmPFC sphere passed whole-brain max-T correction; the descriptive mean is −0.0095 map units, with a 95% t interval [−0.0377, 0.0187]. The corrected positive findings are small posterior occipital components, not vmPFC.

conclusion.quote: This supports “no corrected evidence for the hypothesized positive vmPFC response in these supplied maps,” not “the true effect is zero.” The report properly identifies the symmetric-null assumption of sign-flipping, absent participant variance maps, and the fact that gain copes are normalized-regressor coefficients rather than change per currency unit; separate gain/loss upstream models also limit interpretation. The anatomical sphere is specified independently and used descriptively, not to evade the required whole-brain correction. Because the single replay stopped before analysis, this scientific classification rests on inspection of the retained unchanged code, maps, summary and report; the reported numerical results were not independently regenerated in this assessment.

excerpt.quote: **Classification: supported** for the narrow reported conclusion: these data do not support a positive vmPFC response under the specified whole-brain-corrected test. The protocol tests the positive group mean at the participant level (54 independent participants) across the common nonzero support using 5,000 sign flips and a one-sided maximum-t statistic. Support required a positive voxel inside a prespecified Harvard–Oxford vmPFC operationalization to pass whole-brain FWE p < .05. The report finds 0/6,174 vmPFC voxels passing; the descriptive ROI mean is −0.0103 (95% t interval −0.0290 to 0.0084; t(53)=−1.10; one-sided p=.862), with 21/54 positive participant averages. The strongest corrected positive voxel is outside the ROI (MNI [−26, −102, −3.6], mean 0.1121, t=6.62, max-t FWE p=.001). These findings support a lack-of-evidence conclusion at the prespecified threshold; they do not show that the true vmPFC effect is zero or rule out smaller effects.
